mainEntity.name: How much does a Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI (EA211 Evo), expect £3,000-£5,000 supply-only for a rebuilt unit, or £600-£1,400 for a used engine. Fitting adds approximately £520-£715 labour at UK specialist rates (8-11 hours). Reconditioned units typically sit between used and rebuilt at £1,800-£3,200.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of oil consumption problems in a Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common sign is the oil level warning light illuminating between services, requiring frequent top-ups. Some owners report needing to add 1 litre of oil every 1,000-2,000 miles. Other symptoms include blue smoke from the exhaust on acceleration, fouled spark plugs, and increased carbon buildup on intake valves.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your T-Roc's value and the severity of the failure. T-Roc 1.5 TSI examples typically sit in the £10,000-£33,300 value bracket. On cars worth £10,000+, a rebuilt engine at £3,000-£5,000 is financially viable and carries a 12-month warranty. On sub-£8,000 examples, a used engine at £600-£1,400 plus fitting often makes more sense.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI DADA and DPC engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are 1.5-litre EA211 Evo engines producing 148hp (150 PS). The DADA (2017-2020) was the original 1.5 TSI engine, known for oil consumption issues on early units. The DPC (2020-2024) introduced revised injection and emissions systems. The 2021 facelift brought electronic management and lubrication improvements that made the engine significantly more reliable.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A straight engine swap on a Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI typically takes 8-11 hours labour at a specialist, including transfer of ancillary components. 4Motion all-wheel-drive versions add approximately 1 hour due to driveshaft and haldex system disconnection. Most workshops complete the job in 1-2 working days.

mainEntity.name: Is the Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The EA211 1.5 TSI is generally considered reliable, especially post-2021 facelift models. Early DADA units (2017-2020) have a known oil consumption issue affecting some cars, and low-speed drivability hesitation ('kangarooing') was reported on early examples. The 2021 facelift addressed these issues, making later 1.5 TSI engines significantly more reliable.

historyTimeline.h2: Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI arrived with the first-generation T-Roc (A11/D11) in 2017 as the premium petrol option, positioned above the 1.0 TSI as the engine of choice for buyers wanting Golf-level performance in a compact SUV package. The 1.5 TSI badge has spanned the EA211 Evo and Evo 2 engine families, with continuous refinement through the 2021 facelift and into the current 2024+ production.

milestones.description: First-generation T-Roc (A11/D11) launches with 1.5 TSI DADA engine, 148hp (150 PS), 250Nm torque, featuring Active Cylinder Technology (ACT)
DADA superseded by DPC 1.5 TSI, maintaining 148hp with revised injection and emissions systems
Facelift (MY2022) introduces electronic and lubrication improvements, addressing early oil consumption and drivability concerns
EA211 Evo 2 introduced with gasoline particulate filter, available in 1.5 TSI 148hp guise
Current production continues with DXG 1.5 eTSI mild-hybrid (148hp) for third-generation cars
T-Roc SUV production ends November 2025; cabriolet continues to 2027

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI (EA211 Evo) is generally a reliable modern engine, but early production units (2017-2020 DADA) are known for two primary issues: excessive oil consumption and low-speed drivability concerns sometimes called "kangarooing". The 2021 facelift addressed the worst of these with revised electronic management and lubrication. Rebuilt Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI engines through EnginesMarket include updated components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Excessive Oil Consumption - Why the Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI DADA Wears Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI (DADA - 2017-2020, early EA211 Evo units)
problems.rootCause: The EA211 1.5 TSI uses thinner piston rings with reduced spring pressure to improve fuel economy, which can allow excessive oil to pass into the combustion chamber. Some owners report oil consumption of 0.3 to 0.8 litres per 1,000 kilometres. Volkswagen's own documentation allows up to 1 litre per 2,000km, though many owners consider this excessive.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Revised PCV valve and breather hoses
repairOptions.longevity: First step - sometimes resolves oil consumption on DADA

repairOptions.tier: Oil consumption test & piston ring investigation
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full diagnostic, borescope inspection, compression test
repairOptions.longevity: If PCV replacement doesn't resolve - identifies if rings are the cause

repairOptions.specialistPrice: £3,000-£5,000 (matches Section 4's rebuilt price for EA211 proxy)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, updated piston rings, PCV system, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If oil consumption has caused cylinder scoring or bore damage

problems.recommendation: If your Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI is consuming more than 1 litre of oil per 1,000 miles, start with a PCV system inspection (£250-£400 from a specialist). If oil consumption persists, request a borescope inspection to check for cylinder scoring. If scoring is present, a rebuilt engine with updated piston rings is the definitive fix. Do not wait until low oil pressure warnings appear - by then, bearing damage may have occurred.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt DADA Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI engine prices

problems.h4: Low-Speed Drivability Issues ("Kangarooing") - Why the Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI Hesitates
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI (DADA, DPC - 2017-2021, early EA211 Evo units)
problems.typicalFailureMileage: 10,000-40,000 miles (present from new on affected cars)
problems.rootCause: The 1.5 TSI EA211 Evo engine suffers from a low-speed hesitation or jerking sensation, particularly when pulling away from cold or at low revs. This is believed to be related to the Active Cylinder Technology (ACT) system's cylinder deactivation and fuel mapping interactions.

repairOptions.longevity: First step - many cars resolved by 2021 software update

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, latest ECU calibration, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only if mechanical damage has occurred - very rare for this issue alone

problems.vehicleValueCheck: The hesitation issue is almost always software-related and does not cause mechanical damage. Even on sub-£10,000 T-Roc examples, a £80-£150 software update is a trivial cost relative to vehicle value. Full engine replacement is not justified for drivability issues alone.
problems.recommendation: If your Volkswagen T-Roc 1.5 TSI hesitates at low speed, visit a Volkswagen specialist or main dealer for the latest ECU software update. The 2021 facelift addressed this issue comprehensively. Do not consider engine replacement for drivability hesitation - it's a software problem, not a hardware failure.
